key_insight: ANTAP routes tasks by empirically testing agents' real capabilities and then projecting them with non-textual geometry, making description-based manipulation hard to exploit.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical defense for multi-agent orchestration by replacing vulnerable metadata-based routing with an evaluation-driven mechanism that improves robustness against prompt and embedding attacks.
method: Actively query each agent with capability tests instead of trusting self-descriptions.
Distill results into fixed behavioral operators in a shared semantic space.
Perform routing via algebraic projection, creating a "linguistic firewall" against metadata attacks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports near-zero attack success rate against description-based injection attacks, versus 67.3%+ for the description-based router baseline, and a 20% ASR reduction versus the embedding-based baseline under adaptive embedding attacks.
watch_item: Active testing adds runtime cost and depends on the quality and coverage of the evaluation tasks, which may limit scalability or leave gaps for untested behaviors.
paper_title: Linguistic Firewall: Geometry as Defense in Multi-Agent Systems Routing
